name: DCOPTEST
description: Current simulation approaches for data center cooling system evaluation often require engineers to manually rebuild cooling topologies and control logic for each iteration, which is time consuming. To fill this gap, this paper presents a novel unified virtual testbed and an associated modular approach specifically engineered for design engineers to evaluate diverse cooling topologies. The virtual testbed utilizes high-fidelity emulators implemented in the Modelica language to represent realistic physical dynamics through equation-based model descriptions. These emulators accurately account for the nonlinear, hybrid, and stiff mixed continuous and discrete-time dynamics inherent in complex hydraulic networks. In addition, the virtual testbed adopts a modular method that decouples and standardizes a comprehensive set of heterogeneous cooling topologies and control sequences. This modular method allows engineers to select cooling topologies ranging from legacy air-cooled to advanced liquid-cooled configurations with various control sequences within a single, reconfigurable environment. Ultimately, the virtual testbed automatically executes a comprehensive evaluation of the cooling topology. It assesses strict compliance with ASHRAE thermal guidelines alongside environmental and resource impacts, including energy efficiency, water consumption, and carbon emissions via a multi-objective Key Performance Indicator (KPI) set (PUE, WUE, CUE).
